label: <DEL> step of length-9 sequences starting with i
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (100% of mass), and almost only in length-9 sequences (93% of mass at t=9; the rest is L=8). Within those it is a sparse conjunction-like subset: the first original token i accounts for 72% of mass (lift 38x), and the last original token (prev_tok) q (41% of mass) or z (16%) raises it further. Early tokens such as e/u as the second token and n among the first few also show up in top examples, so it behaves like a weighted sum of several sequence properties. Top examples are all L=9, start with i, end with q/z. It never fires in the original or copy phases, and never for L<=7. Predicate (L=9, <DEL>, starts with i) gets dev F1 0.16, mass recall 0.66. Adding prev_tok in {q,z} raises precision to 0.43 but cuts recall to 0.20. Using just <DEL> & L=9 gets 0.93 mass recall at 0.005 precision.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=i (+5.43), orig2=n (+3.25), prev_tok=q (+2.36), phase=1 & out_tok=j (+2.31), prev_tok=z (+2.16), orig3=n (+1.88). Lower it: orig7=- (-3.13), orig1=3 (-1.95), in_first=0 (-1.94), out_tok=- (-1.75).
